speaker: Kimi K3
text: IGIL's operating margins sit above 55% and revenue grew 31% year-over-year in the September quarter, but the stock has already given back a third of its all-time high and carries a 1.32 beta — so you're paying for quality that the market is still repricing. On the IPO question: with only $10 you can't participate in any US IPO (minimum lots are typically hundreds of dollars) and Indian IPOs require a PAN, demat account, and INR funding, so the practical answer is you wait until the shares list and buy a fractional slice if it's a US name. Buying Reliance on Zerodha delivery costs you roughly 0.38% round-trip (STT, exchange fees, stamp duty, GST, and the ~Rs 16 DP charge per sell day); on Rs 10,000 that's about Rs 38 total, and short-term gains are taxed at 20% if you sell within a year. For auto and battery plays, the US-listed names like TSLA, F, GM, ALB, or ENS are accessible via fractional shares, while Indian names like TATAMOTORS, M&M, EXIDE, or AMARAJA need whole shares under Rs 10,000 — all doable, but each carries very different margin and capital-intensity profiles.

text: IGIL's 52% drawdown and 1.32 beta mean a 35% further drop from here is statistically normal — not a tail event — so any position needs a hard stop at 20% below entry or you're gambling, not investing.
